the willingness of patients to accept training to talk to their offspring about diabetes prevention and risk reduction is high.
the majority of type 1 diabetes patients are willing to accept training in speaking to their offspring to reduce the risk of diabetes.

the willingness of Malaysian type 2 diabetes mellitus patients to be trained to become family health promoters.
the development of a training module to be used by type 2 diabetes mellitus patients to speak to their children to reduce their risk of developing type 2 diabetes.
the willingness of Type 2 diabetes mellitus patients to speak to their children about diabetes prevention and the factors associated with such willingness.

the majority of type 1 diabetes patients were willing accept training to speak with their offspring about diabetes risk and preventive strategies and that a training module should be developed to enhance their knowledge and skills to become effective family health educators.

the majority of type 1 diabetes patients are willing to accept training and this is associated with their family history of type 2 DM, correct knowledge of diabetes risk factor, age > 40, agree that speaking to their children will help to prevent type 1 DM, and being neutral with the statements ‘I have little contact with my offspring, and my offspring are not open for advice’.

the majority of type 1 and type 2 diabetic patients were willing to be trained as health educators.
the Malaysian type 2 diabetes patient population are willing to be trained on how to communicate with their offspring about the risks of diabetes and preventive strategies.
type 2 diabetes patient should be encouraged to be family health educators to their offspring.
The main takeaway from our work is that

type 2 diabetes mellitus patients are generally willing to speak to their family members about diabetes prevention, especially their offspring, but the training module needs to address the barriers that they perceive.
type 2 diabetes is a family disease.
